label: prf:wedderburn-trace-identity
title: Proof of wedderburn trace identity
html:
Proof. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n(R, q) decomposes over the Wedderburn blocks as \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\, \chi^\lambda, where \chi^\lambda is the irreducible character of the block indexed by \lambda and y_\lambda(q) is its Markov weight. Evaluating at the identity and using \chi^\lambda(\mathbf{1}) = d_\lambda = f^\lambda (the ordinary block dimension, the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda) gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1})
    = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\, d_\lambda .

The Markov trace is normalized so that \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}) = 1 (the defining trace condition), whence \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1. The unit sum is the Plancherel completeness of the y_\lambda weights, established for every n from the closed-form recipe for y_\lambda (plancherel_via_recipe).

At q = 1 the Markov weights reduce to y_\lambda = d_\lambda / n!, and the identity becomes the Wedderburn–Artin dimension count \sum_\lambda d_\lambda^2 = n! = \dim H_n for \mathbb{C}[S_n]. \square
